title: The Aftermath of the coast road
premise: Noor Halloran has spent eleven years writing postcards to a burned-down cottage on the coast road, addressed to his childhood friend Elias, who vanished the night of the fire and was never declared dead. When the cottage's new owner finds a box of undelivered letters behind a wardrobe — letters Elias wrote to Noor before the fire, never sent — Noor must finally confront what he knows: that Elias is alive, living under another name two towns over, and chose to disappear from him. The story ends with Noor driving to the coast road one last time, standing at the ruin at dawn, saying goodbye aloud at last — not to Elias's memory, but to the version of himself that needed Elias to come back.
about_author: Orsen Crane is the pen name of a former postal clerk who spent a decade sorting dead letters in a coastal town. Their fiction explores the things people write but never send.

chapters.title: The Address That Burned
chapters.summary: From Noor's POV: we meet him writing postcards with his practiced smile, sending them to an address that no longer exists, and learn the ritual keeps his grief — and his guilt — neatly contained. A stranger named Wren arrives at his door holding a water-stained box found behind a wardrobe in the rebuilt cottage. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a sealed life being opened.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Noor reading Elias's unsent letters and flashbacks to their shared boyhood on the coast road. The letters reveal Elias knew about the fire beforehand — and that Noor said nothing when it mattered. Rising tension as Wren presses for answers and Noor realizes the letters name him directly. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: The Man Under Another Name
chapters.summary: Climax. Noor tracks Elias down — alive, renamed, running a boatyard — and confronts him. Elias admits he staged his disappearance to escape debts and a life that had trapped him, and asks Noor to keep lying, as he always has. Noor must choose between protecting Elias's secret and telling the truth out loud for the first time. Emotional beat: betrayal met with the terrible tenderness of old love.

chapters.title: Goodbye, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Resolution, Noor's POV. He tells Wren the truth, mails the box of letters back to Elias unopened, and drives to the ruined cottage at dawn. Standing where the fire began, he speaks the goodbye he has written a hundred times, releasing both Elias and the self who waited. He writes one final postcard — and keeps it. Emotional beat: belonging redefined as something carried, not awaited.
